source.title: Visual feature integration and the temporal correlation hypothesis

confidence_rationale: Foundational and field-defining review establishing the temporal-correlation (binding-by-synchrony) hypothesis with strong cat/primate gamma-synchrony data. Direction is mixed rather than supports because the hypothesis has been seriously contested since (Shadlen & Movshon 1999 critique; debate over whether synchrony codes or merely accompanies binding). It is strong evidence that dynamic, relational binding via temporal structure is a real candidate mechanism (ARC-006), weaker as proof that synchrony IS the binding code.
failure_signatures: Synchrony may be a by-product of recurrent connectivity rather than the binding code itself (Shadlen & Movshon 1999): a downstream reader needs a mechanism to actually exploit coincidence, or the correlation is epiphenomenal -- the same 'symbol without function' failure mode 641a found in REE's streams.

The hypothesis requires that bound features drive co-varying temporal structure; if a representation's features do not co-vary in time (REE's engineered pre-split z_world), there is no temporal correlation to read.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Features belonging to the same object are bound by the temporal correlation (synchronization, especially in the gamma band) of the neurons that represent them; the relational structure 'these features belong together' is carried by WHEN cells fire relative to each other, not only by WHICH cells fire. Synchrony provides a flexible, on-the-fly grouping code that avoids the combinatorial cost of dedicated conjunction units.
mapping.ree_translation: Directly grounds ARC-006 ('entities are sparse, persistent, BINDABLE structures') by giving a concrete neural proposal for what dynamic binding is, and bears on MECH-044 (relational binding/comparison). It is the historical root of the binding-by-coherence family that the Fries CTC entry generalises, and of REE's MECH-089/MECH-270. It also sharpens the substrate gap: binding-by-synchrony only works if a representation's features genuinely co-vary in time, which REE's engineered, pre-split z_world does not guarantee.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The temporal-correlation hypothesis is contested (Shadlen & Movshon 1999 and successors argue synchrony may accompany rather than constitute binding). It grounds the EXISTENCE of a relational/temporal binding mechanism for ARC-006, not the stronger claim that REE's coherence term is a non-reducible selection factor -- which the V3-EXQ-641a fair-control null specifically failed to demonstrate in the current substrate. Cat/primate visual cortex synchrony does not transfer 1:1 to REE latent streams.
mapping.source_context: Annual Review synthesis of single-unit and multi-unit recordings in cat and monkey visual cortex showing stimulus-specific gamma-band synchronization between neurons coding features of a common object.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (field-defining Annual Review). Mapping fidelity moderate and capped by the ongoing empirical controversy over whether synchrony is the binding code. Transfer risk from visual-cortex spiking to REE latents is real; the contested status is reflected in the 'mixed' direction.
